summary: Describes two TFTP options: one to negotiate the retransmission timeout interval, and one to tell the receiver the transfer size before it begins. It is a draft standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds two options to TFTP requests. One sets how long to wait before retransmission; the other tells the receiver the file size before the transfer begins.

subtitle: Two TFTP options for negotiating a timeout and learning a transfer's size.

tldr.problem: TFTP needed a way to agree on retransmission timing and let the receiving side learn the file size before transfer.
tldr.mechanism: The timeout option carries a wait interval in seconds, while tsize carries a file size in octets; an accepted option is confirmed with an OACK.
tldr.outcome: The receiver can abort a transfer if a file is too large, using Error code 3. RFC 2349 obsoletes RFC 1784 and updates RFC 1350.

today: RFC 2349 is a Draft Standard. It obsoletes RFC 1784 and updates RFC 1350; the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Two TFTP Options
sections.content:
The Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) lets a client get or put a file on a remote host. RFC 2349 describes two options: one for negotiating the timeout interval and one for telling the receiving side the transfer size before it starts.

The options are included in TFTP read-request or write-request packets, using the option extension mechanism described by RFC 2347.
sections.plainLanguage: The options add information to a TFTP file request. They let both sides agree on a timeout or learn the file size before transferring the file.

sections.title: Negotiating the Timeout
sections.content:
The timeout option gives the number of seconds to wait before retransmitting. Its value is sent in ASCII and must be from 1 through 255 inclusive. The option name is case-insensitive.

If the server accepts the option, it replies with an Option Acknowledgment (OACK). The timeout value in the OACK must match the value sent by the client.
sections.plainLanguage: The client proposes how many seconds to wait before sending again. If the server accepts the option, its OACK repeats the same value.

sections.title: Reporting the Transfer Size
sections.content:
The tsize option gives the file size in octets. In a read request, the client sends a size of zero and the server returns the actual size in the OACK. In a write request, the client sends the size and the server echoes it in the OACK.

If the file is too large for the receiving side, that side may abort with an Error packet using error code 3.
sections.plainLanguage: For a read request, the server reports the file size. For a write request, the client reports it. The receiver may stop the transfer if the file is too large.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says basic TFTP has no security mechanism. The described options do not add security, but the RFC states that they do not add additional security risks.
sections.plainLanguage: These options do not add security to TFTP. The RFC says they also introduce no additional security risks.
